# awscc_comprehend_entity_recognizer (Resource)

An Amazon Comprehend custom entity recognizer: a trained model that identifies custom entity types in text, created via an asynchronous training job.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `data_access_role_arn` (String) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that grants Amazon Comprehend read access to your input data.
- `input_data_config` (Attributes) Specifies the format and location of the input data. The S3 bucket containing the input data must be located in the same Region as the entity recognizer being created. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--input_data_config))
- `language_code` (String) The language of the input documents. All documents must be in the same language.
- `recognizer_name` (String) The name given to the entity recognizer.

### Optional

- `model_kms_key_id` (String) ID for the AWS KMS key that Amazon Comprehend uses to encrypt trained custom models.
- `model_policy` (String) The JSON resource-based policy to attach to your custom entity recognizer model.
- `tags` (Attributes Set) Tags to associate with the entity recognizer. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tags))
- `version_name` (String) The version name given to the entity recognizer.
- `volume_kms_key_id` (String) ID for the AWS KMS key that Amazon Comprehend uses to encrypt data on the storage volume attached to the ML compute instance(s).
- `vpc_config` (Attributes) Configuration parameters for an optional private VPC containing the resources you are using for your custom entity recognizer. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--vpc_config))

### Read-Only

- `arn` (String) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies the entity recognizer.
- `id` (String) Uniquely identifies the resource.

<a id="nestedatt--input_data_config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `input_data_config`

Required:

- `entity_types` (Attributes List) The entity types in the labeled training data. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--input_data_config--entity_types))

Optional:

- `annotations` (Attributes) The S3 location of the CSV file that annotates your training documents. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--input_data_config--annotations))
- `augmented_manifests` (Attributes List) A list of augmented manifest files that provide training data for a custom model. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--input_data_config--augmented_manifests))
- `data_format` (String) The format of your training data.
- `documents` (Attributes) The S3 location of the folder that contains the training documents. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--input_data_config--documents))
- `entity_list` (Attributes) The S3 location of the CSV file that has the entity list. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--input_data_config--entity_list))

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = awscc_comprehend_entity_recognizer.example
  identity = {
    arn = "arn"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `arn` (String) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies the entity recognizer

#### Optional

- `account_id` (String) AWS Account where this resource is managed
- `region` (String) Region where this resource is managed

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = awscc_comprehend_entity_recognizer.example
  id = "arn"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
$ terraform import awscc_comprehend_entity_recognizer.example "arn"
```
